topic: Amazon Nova Multimodal Embeddings for cross-modal verification search
question_text: A media company wants analysts to type a text description and retrieve matching clips from an archive of videos, along with related PDFs, images, and audio recordings, to verify claims in AI-generated summaries. The company wants one vector index and one embedding model for all content types, and a single semantic search query path. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Generate transcripts for every file and index them with a text-only embedding model in separate indexes per content type.
Use Amazon Nova Multimodal Embeddings in Amazon Bedrock to embed text, documents, images, video, and audio into a single semantic vector space, and query the one index with embedded text.
Use Amazon Rekognition labels for all content and match analyst queries with keyword search.
Use a different embedding model for each modality and merge result lists with custom ranking code.

explanation: Amazon Nova Multimodal Embeddings produces embeddings for text, documents, images, video, and audio in a unified semantic space, which enables cross-modal queries such as a text query returning video clips from a single index. Transcript-only indexing loses visual content and requires multiple indexes. Rekognition labels with keyword matching cannot capture semantic meaning and does not cover documents or audio. Per-modality models create separate vector spaces that cannot be compared directly and need custom merge logic.
